links.note: how many were to travel by the evening bus -> five; 32177 opens with the five friends' decision
who wrote the piece -> Harishankar Parsai; 32178 is the concept that names Parsai and his reversal of respectful words onto a wreck of a bus
how long after, the Satna bus leaves from Panna -> an hour; 32177 states that connection
which train the bus connects with -- 32177 carries the Panna-Satna-Jabalpur chain. NOTE: this row's marked option is 'Panna ki', while the text says the Jabalpur train
who of the company was aboard -> a partner; 32180 is the hissedar who said the bus would run on its own
which Gandhian movement is invoked -> asahyog; 32181 is the seat's non-cooperation with the body
what he took the green trees for -> enemies; 32184 is 'har ped dushman'
name the lesson and its writer -> 'Bus ki Yatra' by Harishankar Parsai; 32178 names Parsai
the feeling that welled up on seeing the bus -> shraddha; 32178 states that exactly
where he and his friends had to go -> Panna; 32177 is the itinerary concept
why travellers would not ride this bus -- 32179 is the mock-sympathy concept, that it was fit for worship rather than for riding
which train it connects with -> Jabalpur's; 32177
what he means by 'the engine really did start' -> the state of the bus made it a surprise; 32180 is the don't-be-afraid-it-is-experienced exchange
why it felt as if they sat inside the engine -> the noise and vibration; 32182 says exactly that the whole bus seemed to be the engine
which Gandhian movements the passage describes -> both; 32181 names asahyog and savinay avagya
what the passage shows of the bus's condition -> pitiable; 32185 is the bus looking dayaniya in the moonlight
the change in the bus after eight or ten miles -> it settled and ran easily; that settling follows the seat-and-body merger of 32182
the speed it was now doing -> fifteen to twenty miles; 32184 gives that figure
why he had no faith in the bus -> the brakes could fail, the steering break; 32184 word for word
why he took the trees for enemies -> fear of the bus hitting them; 32184
where the fear of drowning came -- part of the same distrust-of-every-part passage, 32184
the scene on both sides of the road -> green trees with birds on them; 32184 describes that very scene
where the bus broke down -> on a puliya; 32187 is the tyre going on the culvert
with what feeling he looked at the company's partner -> shraddha; 32187 records that first respectful look
whose courage and sacrifice was being misused -> the company's partners'; 32188 is the mock-eulogy of the man who died for a tyre
the qualities a revolutionary leader should have -> courage and sacrifice; 32188 is that satire
